decisions.reason: Although the accelerator is less central to the firm's machinery core and likely easier to discontinue than plant-based offerings, its continued home-page visibility and fit with advisory and partnership building make management more likely to justify and continue it than to exit quickly.

As a flagship, publicly emphasized product tied to the firm's circular low-emission direction and likely backed by meaningful R&D spending, the binder is a classic case where management would persist and attribute weak traction to temporary commercialization hurdles.

This decontamination plant is close to the core business, prominently promoted across both years, and framed as a strategic breakthrough, so sunk engineering effort and visible commitment make withdrawal within a year unlikely.
